purpose: Establish system overview, deployment topology, and architectural philosophy.
key_findings: System is a TypeScript SPA aggregating 65+ upstream providers (geopolitics, military, finance, cyber, climate, maritime, aviation) into a unified operational picture.

Deployment topology spans 9 targets: Vercel Edge Functions (SPA + API), Cloudflare (CORS preflight worker), Railway (AIS relay + seed loops + consumer prices), Upstash Redis (cache + stampede protection + rate limit), Convex (contact form + waitlist + entitlements), Mintlify (docs), Tauri (desktop), GHCR (Docker image).

Each platform owns a distinct role — no single platform covers all roles. Split is forced by: WebSocket relay (Railway), edge compute (Vercel), user state + billing (Convex), edge CORS (Cloudflare), local desktop API (Tauri sidecar).
Frontend uses 8-phase init: Storage+i18n → ML Worker → Sidecar → Bootstrap (2-tier concurrent) → Layout → UI → Data → Refresh.
Dual map engine: deck.gl (WebGL flat) + globe.gl (3D globe), with 56 map layer types.
No external state library — AppContext is a central mutable object; URL state syncs bidirectionally via urlState.ts (debounced 250ms).
Proto/RPC contract system: proto/ → buf generate → src/generated/{client,server} + docs/api OpenAPI. sebuf framework with (sebuf.http.config) annotations.
4-layer cache hierarchy: Bootstrap seed (Railway→Redis) → in-memory (per Vercel instance) → Redis (cross-instance, cachedFetchJson coalesces concurrent misses) → upstream API fetch.
6 cache tiers with explicit s-maxage: fast(300s)/medium(600s)/slow(1800s)/static(7200s)/daily(86400s)/no-store(0) + live(60s for energy-atlas tanker positions).
Three CSP sources must stay in sync: index.html <meta>, vercel.json header, src-tauri/tauri.conf.json.
CI has 20+ workflows including mcp-live-smoke.yml (6-hourly, regression net for #4937/#4938), live-api-cache-auth.yml, seed-freshness-monitor.yml (15-min cron).
Pre-push hook runs 7 checks: tsc --noEmit, CJS syntax validation, edge function esbuild bundle check, edge function import guardrail, markdown lint, MDX lint, version sync check.

purpose: Determine how the MCP transport endpoint enforces auth, discovery, and protocol invariants.
key_findings: Architectural invariant #4937: every capability advertised in anonymous `initialize` MUST be anonymously exercisable. A 401 on a gated method hangs MCP SDK transports to their 30s timeout.

publicMethods set is precisely the catalog-enumeration surface: 'tools/list', 'prompts/list', 'resources/list', 'ping', 'logging/setLevel'. This is the agent-readiness scanner's discovery surface before authenticating.
Anonymous methods are the contract; authenticated methods are the value. Splitting them lets agents probe capabilities without credentials, then authenticate only when invoking.
The split is non-negotiable: adding a method to the public set requires verifying it's safely anonymous-callable; removing a method from the public set requires verifying no SDK expects it pre-auth.

purpose: Understand tool execution pipeline, quota enforcement, and the no-refund invariant (GHSA-hcq5).
key_findings: Quota reservation is INCR-first for Pro and user_key contexts: reserveQuota() runs before tool dispatch; on cap-exceeded returns 429 with Retry-After=secondsUntilUtcMidnight; on reservation failure returns 503 (never dispatch on reservation failure).

GHSA-hcq5 invariant: no caller-side rollback of reservation after dispatch. Once tool runs, the daily slot is charged for good. Rationale: '_execute() already incurred the upstream cost, so refunding let a Pro token drive unlimited real cost by always exceeding the budget' and 'refunding let a Pro token bypass the daily cap by driving calls that reliably error after the costly fetch'.
describe_tool is exempt from quota (metadata-only, encouraged by SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS when tools/list entry is ambiguous) but still subject to 60/min rate limiter as abuse guard.
Budget gate: post-JMESPath byte length checked against tool._outputBudgetBytes; on exceed returns _budget_exceeded envelope (not error) with hint — and still no refund (cost is sunk).

cache_all_null guard: if every cache key returned null/undefined, throws 'cache_all_null' (Redis transient/stampede) — structurally distinguishable from 'upstream returned empty list' (which is a JSON value, not null).
Post-filter uses structuredClone of data (not data itself) so a mid-filter throw falls back to pristine full payload, not half-narrowed mutation.
latency_ms is captured AFTER Pro reservation round-trip so P95 error-path dashboard isn't skewed by reservation latency.
HTTP 4xx from internal sibling fetch (e.g. feed-digest HTTP 401) logged at 'warning' (transient HMAC/auth/quota drift); non-HTTP errors and 5xx at 'error'.

purpose: Understand Convex data model, access control, and the hand-rolled distributed locking mechanism.
key_findings: Hand-rolled distributed locking for followed countries: followedCountriesShards (shardId+userId+countryCodes) + followedCountriesCountryLocks (countryCode+lockedUntil+lockId).

Lock is TTL-based (lockedUntil timestamp) with a unique lockId — not using Convex's native transactional model. Implies Convex lacks a primitive that fits the 'lock a country code during a multi-step follow/unfollow' use case.
Entitlement-driven access control: entitlements table is the source of truth for Pro/Enterprise tier gating. checkEntitlementDetailed in gateway.ts reads this.
API keys table with hashed keys — separate from user auth (Clerk sessions). user_key context in dispatch.ts consumes the same daily quota as pro.
The sharding + locking pattern suggests high-concurrency write contention on per-country follow lists — a single followedCountries table would serialize on country code.

purpose: Understand the bulk data hydration endpoint and its 3-tier auth-aware cache policy.
key_findings: Three-tier auth-aware cache policy: isPublicTierBootstrapRequest → 'public, s-maxage=7200, stale-while-revalidate=1800, stale-if-error=7200'; isPublicOnDemandBootstrapRequest → 'public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=600, stale-if-error=3600'; else → 'no-store'.
Public/cacheable vs authenticated/fresh data separation: anonymous public traffic gets long CDN TTLs (2h/1h), authenticated users get no-store (always fresh, never cached).
stale-if-error directives ensure the CDN can serve stale data even when upstream Redis is temporarily unreachable — a graceful degradation mechanism.
Reads cached keys from Redis in a single batch call (per ARCHITECTURE.md §6) — minimizes Redis round-trips for the 100+ key hydration.

purpose: Understand the concierge routing for A2A and NLWeb endpoints.
key_findings: Token-overlap scoring (deliberately not NLU): transparent, deterministic, white-box debuggable.
Name hits outweigh description hits (3x vs 1x) so 'chokepoint status' lands on get_chokepoint_status, not on every tool whose prose mentions shipping.
QUERY_STOPWORDS set filters generic terms (the, and, for, what, worldmonitor, world, monitor, etc.) — prevents generic queries from matching every tool.
Kept as route-less helper (underscore prefix) so neither A2A nor /ask endpoint's cold-start depends on the other's module-level guards.
Returns top-5 by score with tie-break on name localeCompare — deterministic ordering.

purpose: Understand RFC 9728/8414 agent-readiness metadata discovery and Host spoofing protection.
key_findings: Implements RFC 9728 (protected-resource metadata) and RFC 8414 (authorization-server metadata) — both derive issuer/endpoint origin from request Host.

Host spoofing guard: ALLOWED_HOST regex /^(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)?worldmonitor\.app$/ accepts apex + exactly one DNS label (www, api, tech, finance, ...). Rejects evil.com, worldmonitor.app.evil.com, evilworldmonitor.app, and any host with a port.

Falls back to FALLBACK_ORIGIN (https://worldmonitor.app) for any non-matching host — defense-in-depth: a spoofed Host: evil.com would be reflected into issuer/token_endpoint otherwise, pointing an agent's token exchange at an attacker origin.
guardMetadataMethod: read-only documents — answers CORS preflights, allows GET/HEAD, rejects everything else with 405 + Allow header.

purpose: Understand the route matching strategy and its performance characteristics.
key_findings: Map-based O(1) static route lookup + linear dynamic route scan with {param} segments.
Dynamic routes pre-filter by segmentCount (quick rejection) then per-segment literal-or-wildcard match.
Path normalization: trailing slash stripped (except root) — /users/ and /users hit the same handler.
allowedMethods(): for 405 responses, returns sorted methods with implicit HEAD on GET. This is RFC 7231 compliance.
No regex compilation — segments are compared as literal strings or null wildcards. Keeps the matcher cheap and predictable.

purpose: Understand the domain gateway factory pipeline, cache tier headers, and internal-MCP HMAC replay protection.
key_findings: createDomainGateway(routes) is a 10-step pipeline: Origin check → CORS → OPTIONS preflight → API key validation → Rate limiting (endpoint-specific then global) → Route matching (static Map then dynamic scan) → POST-to-GET compat → Handler execution with error boundary → ETag generation (FNV-1a) + 304 → Cache header application.

Per-domain Edge Function bundling rationale (comment): 'Splitting domains into separate edge functions means Vercel bundles only the code for one domain per function, cutting cold-start cost by ~20×.'
8 cache tiers with explicit 3-layer CDN policy: browser (max-age) → CF edge (s-maxage) → Vercel CDN (CDN-Cache-Control). 'live' tier (60s) added for energy-atlas live-tanker map layer.
Internal-MCP HMAC replay protection: claimInternalMcpReplayNonce() uses Redis SET NX with TTL to detect replayed nonces. Returns 'fresh' / 'replay' / 'unavailable'.

MAX_INTERNAL_MCP_BODY = 256KB cap on internal-MCP request bodies — applied at both trust-marker strip block and HMAC-verify block. Both Content-Length AND post-buffer byte count checked (Content-Length can be absent/wrong for chunked bodies).
Idempotency support: beginIdempotency/peekIdempotency with IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER + IDEMPOTENT_REPLAYED_HEADER — clients can retry safely.
Direct LLM quota: DIRECT_LLM_DAILY_QUOTA_LIMIT + reserveDirectLlmQuota — separate from MCP quota, gates direct LLM gateway paths.
Usage scope: runWithUsageScope + deliverUsageEvents — per-request usage events with derived country/region/city/IP/UA/originKind for billing analytics.

purpose: Understand Convex HTTP entry, CORS handling, and error code extraction.
key_findings: Convex httpRouter exposes webhook handlers (payments, Resend) and user-prefs writes.
TRUSTED origins: worldmonitor.app, *.worldmonitor.app, localhost:3000. matchOrigin supports wildcard subdomain matching.
timingSafeEqualStrings: uses HMAC-SHA256 to compare strings in constant time — prevents timing attacks on origin/secrets.
ConvexError data serialization quirk: Convex runtime serializes err.data to JSON string before re-throwing across function boundary. parseConvexErrorData handles both '
' (string) and '{"code":"X",…}' (object) shapes.
SetPreferencesResult: 4 outcomes — ok with syncVersion / CONFLICT with actualSyncVersion / BLOB_TOO_LARGE / RATE_LIMITED. Optimistic concurrency control via syncVersion.

purpose: Establish product positioning, tech stack, and programmatic access surfaces.
key_findings: 6 site variants from single codebase: world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, energy — each on its own subdomain.
4 SDKs (Python, Ruby, Go, npm CLI) + MCP server + REST API + desktop app (Tauri 2) — multi-surface distribution.
Agent discovery files: llms.txt, .well-known/agent-skills/index.json, .well-known/api-catalog — first-class agent-readiness.

Tech stack: Vanilla TypeScript + Vite, globe.gl + Three.js, deck.gl + MapLibre GL, Tauri 2 (Rust) with Node.js sidecar, Ollama/Groq/OpenRouter, Transformers.js (browser-side), Protocol Buffers (281 protos, 35 services), sebuf HTTP annotations.
AGPL-3.0-only license — commercial use permitted under copyleft compliance.
Smithery badge + skills.sh badge — MCP server is listed on smithery.ai and skills.sh.

purpose: Understand Vercel middleware: bot filtering, routing, and social preview handling.
key_findings: Middleware filters automated traffic: blocks known crawler user-agents on API and asset paths.
Allows social preview bots (Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Telegram, Discord) on story and OG endpoints — these are the only bots that get through.
Runs before Edge Functions — first line of defense after CDN.
